reuse.why: Every rule change goes into the existing shared getScheduledAmount, the tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules, and the API field calls the same helper.

duplication.why: No logic is copied; the old midpoint variants are removed rather than kept alongside the new rule.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule stays in shared/schedules.ts, and callers only pass their own amount and operator.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field, apart from an unrelated import reorder in schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: A single definition owns the rule, but the operator is an optional trailing argument, so the desktop-client callers (Balance, SchedulesTable, mobile lists) that omit it silently skip the approximate-amount rule.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount (shared/schedules.ts): the rangeRounding parameter is replaced by an op parameter and an isapprox branch is added; core callers pass op, while desktop-client callers still call it without op
